title: Lean Muscle Mass Isn’t a Cure-All for Metabolic Health - Nautilus
gist: LSU researchers analyzing ~60,000 UK Biobank adults with MRI/X-ray-measured fat-free mass report findings that challenge the conventional wisdom that lean muscle mass broadly protects metabolic health; specifics are not in the excerpt.

insights.claim: A study in The Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism challenges the conventional wisdom that building lean muscle mass reliably protects metabolic health, including against diabetes.
entities: The Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism
insights.so_what: Could temper fitness/body-composition health claims and inform metabolic-drug positioning (e.g., muscle-preservation narratives).
insights.speaker: Jake Currie

insights.claim: Louisiana State University researchers analyzed data from close to 60,000 U.K. Biobank adults aged 37–73 whose fat-free mass, a proxy for lean muscle, was measured by MRI and low-level X-ray scans.
insights.so_what: Large imaging cohort lends weight to the finding.
insights.locator: A team of nutritional and chronic
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
